task_production_rates.name: Inspect Floor Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk and inspect floor protection covering. Check for tears, lifted edges. Fast visual inspection.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Major tears or exposed areas identified and patched
defect_tolerance.QT3: Any visible tears or gaps repaired, edges secure
defect_tolerance.QT4: All protection secure, seams taped, no gaps
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect coverage, all seams reinforced

task_production_rates.name: Mask Baseboard Top Edge
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply masking tape along baseboard top edge. Press firmly for seal. Standard blue tape at QT2-QT3, green edge-seal at QT4+.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Green edge-seal tape with damp rag technique, perfect seal
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect seal for crisp line, no bleed-through possible

task_production_rates.name: Mask Door Casing Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply masking tape along door casing edges adjacent to walls. Slightly slower than baseboard due to vertical orientation and corners.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean tape line around all door edges
defect_tolerance.QT4: Green edge-seal tape, perfect corners
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect seal at all corners and edges

task_production_rates.name: Mask Window Casing Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply masking tape along window casing edges adjacent to walls.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean tape line around all window edges
defect_tolerance.QT4: Green edge-seal tape, perfect corners
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect seal at all corners and edges

task_production_rates.name: Mask Wall Fixtures
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify or apply masking to outlets, switches, wall fixtures. ~6 items per room average. ~15 min per room.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All fixtures masked, no major gaps
defect_tolerance.QT3: All fixtures fully masked and sealed
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect masking, tape edges sealed
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect masking, all edges sealed

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Primed Wall Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of primed walls with work light. Mark imperfections. Faster than ceiling (no overhead). Per PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference: wall inspect QT3 = 800 SF/hr, but this is post-prime inspection which is faster.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Identify visible imperfections: nail pops, dings, scratches, drips

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Primed Wall Surface (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Detailed inspection with bright work light, marking all defects including minor imperfections.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Comprehensive defect identification under bright light

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Primed Wall Surface (Critical)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Critical inspection with raking light, multiple passes. Satin/semi-gloss finishes reveal all imperfections.

defect_tolerance.QT5: All defects identified under raking light. Satin/semi-gloss is unforgiving.

task_production_rates.name: Spackle Wall Imperfections
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spackle application on walls. Faster than ceiling (no overhead fatigue). Rate reflects typical defect density on primed walls.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Fill all marked defects, reasonable feathering
defect_tolerance.QT4: Fill all defects with careful feathering for invisible repairs

task_production_rates.name: Spackle Wall Imperfections (Critical)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Critical spackle work with wide feathering, multiple thin coats. Slower for satin/semi-gloss surface prep.

defect_tolerance.QT5: Wide feathering, multiple thin coats. Perfect surface required.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Spackled Areas on Wall
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pole sander on spackled areas, blend into surrounding surface. Faster than ceiling work.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Sand and blend, repair should not telegraph
defect_tolerance.QT4: Sand perfectly smooth, repair should be invisible

task_production_rates.name: Sand Spackled Areas on Wall (Critical)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Critical sanding to perfection, wet sponge test. No imperfections acceptable for satin/semi-gloss.

defect_tolerance.QT5: Sand to perfection, wet sponge test. No imperfections acceptable.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Prime Spackled Areas on Wall
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot prime spackled areas with brush to seal repairs before finish coat. Prevents flashing.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Spot prime all repairs, feather edges
defect_tolerance.QT5: Spot prime all repairs with wide feather, may need light sand after

task_production_rates.name: Dust Wipe Wall Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Wipe walls with damp cloth or tack cloth to remove dust before finish coat.

defect_tolerance.QT4: All dust removed, surface clean
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect dust removal, tack cloth follow-up

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Entire Primed Wall
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pole sander with 220 grit, light even pass. Walls are faster than ceiling (no overhead). Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_PREP_SAND_LIGHT = 400 SF/hr, adjusted up for wall position.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light even pass over entire wall, focus on nibs or imperfections

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Entire Primed Wall (Critical)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Thorough sanding with raking light inspection. Critical for satin/semi-gloss finishes.

defect_tolerance.QT5: Thorough even sanding with raking light inspection. Satin/semi-gloss shows every imperfection.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Sanding Dust from Wall
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: HEPA vacuum with brush attachment. Walls faster than ceiling (no overhead).

defect_tolerance.QT4: Thorough vacuum of entire wall
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete vacuum of entire wall, tack cloth follow-up recommended

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Ceiling Line
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Angled brush cut-in at ceiling line. WALL PAINTER ESTABLISHES THE CEILING LINE. Freehand cut-in, no tape. Base 100 LF/hr adjusted for QT2 economy pace. Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_CUTIN_CEILING base = 100 LF/hr, QT2 = 130 LF/hr.

QT4.notes: Careful pace, clean line no visible wobble at 3 feet

QT5.notes: Critical pace, crisp line no visible wobble at arm's length

defect_tolerance.QT2: Acceptable if neat, minor wobble OK at distance
defect_tolerance.QT3: Reasonably straight line, minor wobble acceptable at distance
defect_tolerance.QT4: Clean line, no visible wobble at 3 feet
defect_tolerance.QT5: Crisp line, no visible wobble at arm's length

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Ceiling Line (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat cut-in at ceiling line. Same technique as first coat.

QT3.notes: Match first coat line, improve any wobbles

QT4.notes: Clean line, no visible wobble at 3 feet

QT5.notes: Crisp line, perfect match to first coat

defect_tolerance.QT3: Match first coat line, improve any wobbles
defect_tolerance.QT4: Clean line, no visible wobble at 3 feet
defect_tolerance.QT5: Crisp line, perfect match to first coat

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Cut in wall paint at baseboard, door casing, window casing tape lines. Cut into tape edge for clean reveal. Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_CUTIN_TRIM QT3 = 90 LF/hr; this is faster because cutting to tape.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Precise cut to tape line
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect cut to tape line

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat cut-in at trim edges. Same technique as first coat.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Precise cut to tape line
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect cut to tape line

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Spray Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Cut-in at trim tape lines for spray-only method. Same brush technique as roll and spray_backroll cut-in. Spray-only limited to QT2-QT3.

task_production_rates.name: Roll Wall Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 9-inch roller with extension pole. Wall finish is ~15-20% faster than ceiling (no overhead). Ceiling finish roll R1 = 280 SF/hr, so wall = ~330-340 SF/hr. Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_WALL_ROLL_FINISH_1 QT3 = 380 SF/hr. Rate is CONSTANT across all quality tiers â€” application is a binary task.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage, minor lap marks acceptable
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, no visible lap marks
defect_tolerance.QT5: Critical application â€” uniform coverage, perfect technique

task_production_rates.name: Roll Wall Finish Coat 1 (Textured)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Textured walls require more product and slower application. Base smooth rate / texture modifier (1.15 for knockdown).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage on texture, minor holidays acceptable
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, all texture valleys filled
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect coverage on texture, no visible holidays

task_production_rates.name: Roll Wall Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat is faster per COAT_FINISH_2 modifier (0.90). Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_WALL_ROLL_FINISH_2 QT3 = 445 SF/hr.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage, blend with first coat
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, no visible lap marks, consistent sheen
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect coverage, flawless technique

task_production_rates.name: Spray Wall Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray on walls, coupled to backroll rate. SPRAY RATE MUST BE <= BACKROLL RATE per doctrine. Backroll is bottleneck at 390 SF/hr, so spray paced to match. Per Production Rate Reference with spray/backroll coupling.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, consistent mil thickness
defect_tolerance.QT5: Critical spray application â€” perfect overlap, consistent mil thickness

task_production_rates.name: Backroll Wall Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 18-inch roller on walls sets pace for spray+backroll system. THIS IS THE BOTTLENECK. Walls ~15-20% faster than ceiling (ceiling backroll = 320 SF/hr, so wall = ~390 SF/hr). Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_WALL_BACKROLL_PRIME = 450 SF/hr (primer is faster), finish slightly slower.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Thorough backroll, uniform sheen
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect backroll technique â€” uniform finish critical

task_production_rates.name: Spray Wall Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second spray coat, slightly faster per COAT_FINISH_2 modifier. Still coupled to backroll rate.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage, blend with first coat
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage, consistent technique
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect application â€” flawless finish

task_production_rates.name: Backroll Wall Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second backroll coat, slightly faster than first per COAT_FINISH_2 modifier (0.90).

defect_tolerance.QT4: Thorough backroll, uniform finish
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect backroll â€” flawless sheen uniformity required

task_production_rates.name: Spray Wall Finish (No Backroll)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray-only on walls, no backroll coupling constraint. Higher overlap required. Walls ~15-20% faster than ceiling spray-only (ceiling = 550 SF/hr). QT2/QT3 only â€” controlled conditions.

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Between Finish Coats
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light sand first finish coat with 220 grit pole sander before second coat. Walls faster than ceiling (ceiling = 500 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light even pass to smooth nibs before second coat

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Between Finish Coats (Critical)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Careful sanding with inspection under work light. Critical for satin/semi-gloss finishes. Walls faster than ceiling (ceiling = 350 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.QT5: Careful sanding with inspection between coats. Critical for satin/semi-gloss.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Intercoat Sanding Dust
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Vacuum sanding dust before second coat. Walls faster than ceiling (ceiling = 600 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.QT4: All dust removed before second coat
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete dust removal, tack cloth follow-up

task_production_rates.name: Remove Trim Masking Tape
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove masking tape from trim edges. Pull at angle for clean release. Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_UNMASK_ALL = 400 LF/hr.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Tape removed, minor paint chips OK
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean tape removal, no paint damage
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect tape removal, no edge damage
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect tape removal, crisp paint line revealed

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Floors
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shop vacuum of floors to remove paint drips and debris from wall painting.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Thorough vacuum, area clean
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete cleanup, inspection-ready

task_production_rates.name: Remove Wall Fixture Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove tape and paper/plastic from wall fixtures. Faster than setup.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Protection removed cleanly
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect removal, fixtures clean

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time per job to clean brushes, rollers, spray equipment with water.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Tools thoroughly cleaned
defect_tolerance.QT5: Tools thoroughly cleaned and stored

task_production_rates.name: Final Wall Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of completed wall work. QT2: Quick visual for major misses at 6ft, ambient lighting. QT3: Thorough visual, address visible defects. Walls faster than ceiling (no overhead).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Quick visual for major misses only â€” holidays, drips, sags

task_production_rates.name: Final Wall Inspection (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Detailed inspection with work light. Touch up any defects. Walls faster than ceiling (ceiling = 1200 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.QT4: Detailed inspection with work light, perfect finish expected

task_production_rates.name: Final Wall Inspection (Critical)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Critical inspection under raking light for satin/semi-gloss finish. Any imperfection must be addressed. Walls faster than ceiling (ceiling = 800 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.QT5: Critical inspection under raking light. Satin/semi-gloss is less forgiving than flat.

modifiers.notes: Standard residential wall height. Floor-level access.
Taller walls require step/extension ladder for cut-in at ceiling. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
May require scaffolding. Significant productivity impact. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Scissor lift or scaffolding tower required. Major equipment setup. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Baseline smooth primed wall
Light texture increases surface area ~15%, slows application ~10%. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Moderate texture increases surface area ~20%, slows application ~15%. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Economy tier - reduced prep, faster pace. Scope reduction not rate increase. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Baseline for all rates. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Premium tier - more thorough execution, tighter tolerances. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Superior tier - maximum care, critical inspection. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Occupied sensitive space requires extra care. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Occupied space, crew handles protection. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Cold conditions affect dry time and application. Per research.json site_condition_analysis.
Hot conditions require faster work to maintain wet edge. Per research.json site_condition_analysis.
First finish coat slightly slower. Per PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference.
Second finish coat faster. Per PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference.
Flat/matte is forgiving on walls â€” baseline application time
Eggshell slightly less forgiving than flat. Per PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference MAT_EGGSHELL.
Satin shows more imperfections. QT4+ required. Per PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference MAT_SATIN.
Semi-gloss magnifies imperfections. QT5 only for drywall walls. Per PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference MAT_SEMI.

quality_tier_effects.description: Economy wall finish â€” single coat, minimal prep
quality_tier_effects.notes: QT2 SCOPE REDUCTION: Skip entire inspection/repair module. Skip full-surface sanding. Single coat only (cut-in + roll/spray, no coat 2). Final inspection is quick visual at 6ft. IMPORTANT: Application quality (no drips/sags/holidays) is NOT reduced. Sheen limited to flat/matte/eggshell.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard wall finish â€” baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard NC: inspection/repair module, two coats default (1 coat acceptable if coverage achieved), thorough final check. Flat/matte/eggshell available.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium wall finish â€” two coats with intercoat sanding
quality_tier_effects.notes: Premium: thorough prep, light sand full wall before finish, two coats mandatory with intercoat sanding, detailed inspection. Flat through satin available.

quality_tier_effects.description: Superior wall finish â€” two coats, critical prep and inspection
quality_tier_effects.notes: Critical work: meticulous prep with raking light, full sand primed wall, two coats mandatory with intercoat sanding, critical final inspection. Semi-gloss available (QT5 only for drywall).

sheen_quality_tier_gates.notes: Lower sheens hide imperfections; available at any quality tier
Satin reveals imperfections; requires enhanced prep and sanding discipline
Semi-gloss magnifies imperfections on drywall; requires meticulous workmanship. Per materials.json research correction RC-006.
Gloss is NOT available for drywall walls. Not a real-world application. Per materials.json research correction RC-005.

texture_effects.notes: Orange peel texture increases surface area ~15%, slows application ~10%
Knockdown texture increases surface area ~20%, slows application ~15%

height_effects.notes: Standard residential wall height. Extension pole from floor for most tasks.
Step/extension ladder required for ceiling line cut-in. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
May require scaffolding for some tasks. Per Modifier_Registry.md.
Scissor lift or scaffolding tower required. Major equipment setup. Per Modifier_Registry.md.

coupling_constraints.description: When using spray+backroll on walls, spray rate must not exceed backroll rate. Backroller sets the pace.
coupling_constraints.practical_implication: Spray at 390 SF/hr, backroll at 390 SF/hr means effective wall rate is 390 SF/hr per crew (sprayer + backroller in tandem)
coupling_constraints.notes: Per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine Â§ Spray/Backroll Throughput Coupling. Spray and backroll done by 2-person crew working in tandem, bottleneck is backroll.

crew_configurations.name: Wall Roller
crew_configurations.notes: One person does cut-in and rolling with extension pole

crew_configurations.name: Spray + Backroll Wall Crew
crew_configurations.notes: Sprayer and backroller work in tandem. Backroller sets pace. NC production standard.

crew_configurations.name: Single Sprayer
crew_configurations.notes: Spray-only wall application, one person. QT2/QT3 only in controlled conditions.

wall_vs_ceiling_factor.description: Wall work is inherently faster than equivalent ceiling work due to no overhead fatigue, neck angle, or arm positioning issues
wall_vs_ceiling_factor.notes: Wall rates are approximately 15-20% faster than equivalent ceiling work rates. Per brief Section 9 and PaintFactor_Production_Rate_Reference: POS_WALL = 1.0 vs POS_CEILING = 1.15.

assumptions.value: Wall rates ~15-20% faster than ceiling rates
assumptions.note: Wall position modifier POS_WALL = 1.0 vs ceiling POS_CEILING = 1.15

assumptions.value: Using Modifier_Registry H1=1.0, H2=1.30, H3=1.50, H4=2.00
assumptions.note: Brief suggested wall-specific lighter values (1.15/1.3/1.5) but Modifier_Registry is authoritative per Doctrine Authority Rule

assumptions.value: Wall painter establishes ceiling line via freehand cut-in
assumptions.note: Critical difference from ceiling spec â€” ceiling painter rolled freely, wall painter creates clean line

assumptions.value: Gloss sheen NOT available for drywall walls
assumptions.note: Gloss on drywall is not a real-world application

risks.description: Wall height modifier values may need wall-specific calibration
risks.context: Brief suggested lighter values for walls (1.15/1.3/1.5 vs registry 1.30/1.50/2.00) due to no overhead fatigue. Using registry values pending doctrine update.
risks.mitigation: Flag for field calibration. App allows rate adjustment.

risks.description: Trim masking rates may vary by trim profile complexity
risks.context: Flat masking at baseboard is faster than masking around ornate door casing
risks.mitigation: Rates reflect average trim complexity. Adjust for ornate trim via complexity modifier.

risks.description: Ceiling line cut-in rate depends on painter skill
risks.context: Freehand ceiling line cut-in is skill-dependent. QT-scaled rates assume journeyman skill level.
risks.mitigation: QT rates provide progressive tolerance. Field calibration recommended.

validation_plan.method: Time journeyman on freehand ceiling line cut-in, standard height wall
Time 2-person spray+backroll crew on smooth wall, measure net SF/hr
Time single roller on standard wall, measure by coat
Time tape application along trim edges, distinguish baseboard from casing
Compare cut-in and roll rates at standard vs tall wall heights

uncertainties.description: Brief states wall height modifiers should be lighter than ceiling (1.15/1.3/1.5 vs 1.30/1.50/2.00) due to no overhead fatigue. Using Modifier_Registry standard values as canonical per Doctrine Authority Rule.
uncertainties.current_approach: Using Modifier_Registry values: H1=1.0, H2=1.30, H3=1.50, H4=2.00
uncertainties.notes: Consider adding wall-specific height modifiers to Modifier_Registry if field calibration confirms lighter values are appropriate
